info.name: FinTechNerdCon Backend
info.description:
Front-end API collection for the FinTechNerdCon Supabase backend.

Mirrors postman/API.md. Two kinds of endpoint:

- `/functions/v1/...` edge functions. verify-email, register, login, forgot-password, reset-password and config are public (anon key only); `user/profile` and the `admin/*` routes need the access token from login
- `/rest/v1/...` auto-generated REST over the tables, guarded by row-level security — needs the access token from login

## Setup

1. Import the environment file next to this collection (`FinTechNerdCon.postman_environment.json`) and select it.
2. For a deployed project set `base_url` to `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co` and `anon_key` to the project's anon/publishable key.
3. Run **1. Auth → Login**. Its test script stores `access_token`, `refresh_token` and `user_id` as collection variables, so every later request is authenticated automatically.

The collection sends `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` by default; the public endpoints override this with no auth.

Assertions accept every status the API documents for a request (e.g. Register passes on 201, 403 and 409), so a full collection run stays green whether or not the test email is on the attendee list.

variable.description: Second guild for the 1..3 selection used by Register and Update my profile.
Set by GET user/profile — the caller's badge number, e.g. 00427.
Set by the connection request / list requests tests.
A slug from `select * from public.mint_qr_codes(...)`. Printed as https://<app>/q/<slug>.
An agenda id with is_invite_only = true. Captured by 'Agenda (filtered)' when one exists.

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Register, login and session handling. All public — anon key only, no bearer token.

request.description:
Registration is invite-only — the email must already be in `email_stack`. Case-insensitive and trimmed.

| Parameter | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| email | string | yes |

Every response has the same three keys: `status` (`Success`/`Error`), `message`, `data`.

```json
{
  "status": "Success",
  "message": "This email is on the attendee list.",
  "data": { "email_exist": true }
}
```

- **200** `Success` with `data.email_exist: true` — on the list
- **200** `Success` with `data.email_exist: false` — not on the list. A miss is not an error: the lookup worked, the answer is just no. Branch on `data.email_exist`
- **400** `Error` — email missing, or the body isn't JSON
- **405** `Error` — must be POST
- **500** `Error` — lookup failed

`data` is `null` on every error path, so the three keys are always safe to read.

Optional pre-screen: Register runs the same check itself and returns 403 `email_in_stack: false` when the email isn't on the list.

The SQL helper behind this (`public.verify_email`) is granted to the service role only, so this function is the only way to ask the question.

exec: console.log(pm.variables.get('test_email') + ' is not on the attendee list — Register will return 403.');

request.description:
| Parameter | Type | Required | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| email | string | yes | Valid email, must be on the attendee list |
| password | string | yes | Min 8 characters |
| first_name | string | yes | Non-empty |
| last_name | string | yes | Non-empty |
| guild_ids | integer[] | **yes** | 1 to 3 guilds.id values. A single `guild_id` is still accepted as a one-guild selection |
| user_type_config_id | integer | no | configs.id where type = 'user_type' |
| company_name | string | no | |
| job_title | string | no | |
| profile_image | string | no | URL |
| device_type | integer | no | Push delivery |
| device_token | string | no | FCM/APNs token |

Responses:

- **201** — created; body is `{ success, message }` only, with no session or profile
- **403** `email_in_stack: false` — not on the attendee list, nothing created
- **409** — already registered, send the user to Login
- **400** — missing/invalid field, password under 8 chars, no guilds or more than 3, bad guild_ids/user_type_config_id

Register hands back nothing but the status and message — run Login next to get the token.

Guilds are chosen at sign-up: at least 1, at most 3. Nothing is created if the selection is rejected.

exec: console.log('Registered. Run Login next for the token.');

request.description:
| Parameter | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| email | string | yes |
| password | string | yes |

Responses:

- **200** `{ success, message, data: { token, token_type, expires_in, expires_at, refresh_token, user } }`
- **401** `Invalid email or password.` — returned for both a wrong password and an unknown email, on purpose. Do not try to tell them apart in the UI
- **400** — email or password missing
- **405** — must be POST

The test script stores `access_token`, `refresh_token` and `user_id` for the rest of the collection.

Step 1 of the password reset — emails a 6-digit code.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| email | string | yes | Case-insensitive, trimmed |
| redirect_to | string | no | Only for the web/link variant |

- **200** `{ status: "Success", message, data: { email_sent: true } }`
- **400** `Error` — email missing or malformed
- **429** `Error` — per-address email throttle; the message names the wait

**An unknown email also returns 200.** Deliberate: any other response would let someone discover which addresses have accounts. So the UI should say "check your email" and must not branch on whether the account exists.

Locally the mail lands in Mailpit: http://127.0.0.1:54324 — copy the 6-digit code into the `reset_code` variable, then send **Reset password**.

Note each new request invalidates the previous code, so a whole-folder run can't finish the reset in one pass: this request re-issues the code before Reset password runs. Send the two by hand, in order.

exec: console.log('Check Mailpit (http://127.0.0.1:54324) for the code, then set the reset_code variable.');

request.description:
Step 2 — exchanges the code for a new password. Owning the code is the authorisation, so no session is needed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| email | string | with `token` | Address the code was sent to |
| token | string | yes* | The 6-digit code from the email |
| token_hash | string | yes* | Instead of email+token: the `token` query param from the emailed link (web flow) |
| password | string | yes | New password, min 8 characters |

\* Send either `email` + `token`, or `token_hash` alone.

- **200** `{ status: "Success", message, data: { token, token_type, expires_in, expires_at, refresh_token, user } }` — `data` matches Login's, and the test script stores the session
- **400** `Error` — invalid/expired/used code, password under 8 chars, missing fields, or "New password should be different from the old password."
- **405** `Error` — must be POST

Codes are single-use; wrong, used and expired all share one message on purpose. Requesting a new code invalidates the previous one, so use the newest email.

Skipped unless `reset_code` is set — fill it in from the email that **Forgot password** triggers, then send this request on its own (a folder run would re-issue the code first and invalidate it).

**This changes the account's password.** Afterwards `test_password` is stale — set it to `new_password` (or reset it back), otherwise Login will start failing.

Guards and chained values are read with `pm.variables.get`, so `reset_code` works whether you set it as a collection variable, an environment variable, or with `newman --env-var`.

exec: console.log('reset_code not set — skipping. Run Forgot password, take the code from the email, set reset_code, then send this.');
console.log('Password changed to new_password. Update test_password to match, or Login will now fail. reset_code cleared — codes are single-use.');

request.description:
Access tokens expire after 1 hour (`expires_in`). Handled automatically by supabase-js when you call `setSession` — this request is the raw equivalent for clients that store tokens themselves.

Returns a fresh `access_token` and `refresh_token`; the old refresh token is consumed.

Revokes the session (`supabase.auth.signOut()` in the app). Returns 204.

Skipped unless `allow_destructive` is `true`, so a whole-collection run doesn't end the session the later folders depend on. Send it on its own whenever you like.

exec: console.log('Skipping Logout — set allow_destructive to true to run it.');

item.name: 2. Config
item.description:
Lookup lists for pickers. Public — the register screen needs guilds and user types before the user has a token.

Keys in `data` are the literal `configs.type` values, so hyphenated ones need bracket access: `data["event-quest"]`.

Responses carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` — fetch once at app start.

request.description:
Every lookup list in one call:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "guilds":      [{ "id": 1, "name": "AI & Agentic Systems", "description": null }],
    "user_type":   [{ "id": 1, "name": "Builder", "description": "I create products, tools, and systems." }],
    "event-quest": [{ "id": 4, "name": "Main Quests", "description": null }],
    "event-day":   [{ "id": 8, "name": "Day 0", "description": null }],
    "stage-type":  [{ "id": 11, "name": "Stage 1", "description": null }]
  }
}
```

Every row is `{ id, name, description }`; `description` is only set for `user_type` today and null elsewhere.

Ids are one shared sequence across all types, so always match on `type` + `id`, never `id` alone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| type | string | no | Comma-separated `configs.type` values. Ignored if a path segment is given |

Unlike the path form, an unknown value here returns `{"nope": []}` with 200 rather than 404, so one bad entry doesn't derail a multi-type request.

item.name: 3. Profile, people & connections
item.description:
My profile, the attendee directory, connection requests and guild membership — all through the `user` edge function, which resolves the caller from the bearer token.

Run them in order the first time: People (directory) stores `other_user_id` for the profile and connection requests.

Direct REST equivalents (filtering the users table yourself) are documented in postman/API.md §4.7; only "Delete my account" is kept here, because no function covers it yet.

request.description:
Everything a profile screen needs in one call, in the { status, message, data } envelope:

- the editable columns
- `nerd_number` — the badge number, e.g. "00427", issued at registration and never editable
- `user_type` as `{ id, name, description }` (null when unset), plus `guilds` — the user's 1 to 3 guilds in the same shape
- `profile_image` as a full public URL (or null)
- `total_xp` and `rank` from the leaderboard — 0 / null until a mission is completed

The row is resolved from the bearer token, so there is no id to pass. 401 if the token is missing or expired (the anon key alone is not enough).

formdata.description: 1 to 3 guilds. Repeat this row per guild, or send one comma-separated value (2,3).
Second guild. Untick both rows to keep the current selection.
Select a JPEG/PNG/WebP/HEIC under 5 MB. Leave it unselected to keep the current picture.

request.description:
Partial update of my own profile, as multipart/form-data so the picked image goes in the same request. Do not set Content-Type by hand — Postman adds the boundary.

Editable fields (all optional, send only what you are changing):

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| first_name | Cannot be empty |
| last_name | Cannot be empty |
| user_type_config_id | `configs.id` where type = 'user_type' — from GET All config |
| guild_ids | 1 to 3 `guilds.id` values — repeat the row per guild, or send `2,3` in one value. Replaces the whole selection; it cannot be emptied, so untick to keep the current one |
| company_name | Empty value clears it |
| job_title | Empty value clears it |
| profile_image | File part. Uploaded to the `profile-images` bucket under `<user-id>/<timestamp>.<ext>`; the saved value is its public URL and the previous upload is deleted |

Untick a row to leave that field alone. A form cannot carry null, so an empty value (or the literal `null`) clears an optional field, and an unselected file part means "keep the current picture".

nerd_number, email and is_admin are ignored if sent — they are not the user's to change. device_type / device_token are not editable here either; patch those on `/rest/v1/users?id=eq.{{user_id}}`.

The response is the same shape as GET My profile, so the screen can re-render from it.

## Sending JSON instead

Switch Body to **raw / JSON** and the same fields work, with `null` to clear one. There, `profile_image` takes a data URI (`data:image/jpeg;base64,…`) to upload, an https URL to point at an image hosted elsewhere, or null to remove it.

exec: pm.test('1 to 3 guilds, matching what was sent', () => {
// Only asserted when a file was actually attached to the form.

request.description:
Attendee directory, paged.

- `search` — one term matched against name, nerd number, company and job title ("wasim raza", "00427", "simpalm")
- `user_type` — `all` for every type, or a configs.id (1 Builder, 2 Operator, 3 Explorer)
- `guild_id` — optional, narrows to one guild
- `page` / `per_page` — default 20, max 100

Each card carries `connection.status` (none / pending_sent / pending_received / connected / rejected) so the right button can be drawn without another call. Your own row is never included.

Admin accounts (`is_admin = true`) are event staff and never appear here — nor as a profile / connection / chat target, and not in `pagination.total` either.

exec: // Remember the first person, so the profile / connection requests below have a target.
console.log('No other attendees yet — register a second account to try the connection routes.');

request.description:
Same detail as My profile, plus `connection` (status + request_id) and `is_connected`.

`other_user_id` is set by the People request above. Email is only returned once you are connected.

400 if the id is not a uuid, 404 if there is no such attendee.

exec: console.log('Run People (directory) first to set other_user_id:', body.message);

request.description:
Asks to connect. One row exists per pair, so:

- 409 if you are already connected or have already asked
- asking someone who already asked you **accepts** their request
- a rejected pair can be asked again

The response is the pair's new state: `{ status, request_id }`.

`status=`

- `pending` (default) — requests waiting on **you**
- `sent` — requests you sent, unanswered
- `accepted` — your connections
- `rejected` — answered no

`search` narrows by the other person's name, company, job title or nerd number. Each row is `{ request_id, status, created_at, responded_at, user }`, where `user` is the same card as the directory.

exec: // Pick up an inbox request so Accept / Reject below have something to answer.

request.description:
One route for both answers: send `"action": "accept"` or `"action": "reject"`. `{ "user_id": "..." }` works instead of `request_id`, and `?action=reject` on the query string works instead of putting it in the body.

Only the person who **received** a request can answer it (403 otherwise), and only while it is pending (409 if already answered).

Run "My requests / connections" with status=pending first — its test stores `request_id`.
Every guild, flagged with `is_joined` for the caller, plus `joined_count` and `max_guilds` (3). This is what a "my guilds" picker renders.

One route for both: send `"action": "join"` or `"action": "leave"` (or `?action=leave` on the query string).

Edits the same 1–3 selection the profile shows, and answers with the guilds you belong to afterwards.

409s: already in it / not in it, **at most 3 guilds** on join, and at least 1 on leave.
`user/people` scoped to one guild: same cards, same search / user_type / paging, and it also leaves you out. `guild_id` is required.

**Known gap.** This returns 204 and removes the profile row, but the `auth.users` record survives (the cascade only runs the other way), so that email can never be re-registered.

Don't ship this as the delete-account button — it needs an edge function that removes both.

Skipped unless `allow_destructive` is `true`, so a whole-collection run doesn't wipe your test account.

exec: console.log('Skipping account deletion — set allow_destructive to true to run it.');

item.name: 4. Home
item.description: The Home screen in one call: announcement banner, floor-plan map, and the quick-start card (one item at a time, resolved server-side).

request.description:
Announcement text, `map_image` (floor plan URL, or null), `quick_start` and `stats`.

`quick_start.step` is `save_sessions` until 3 events are on the schedule, then `first_connection` until there is one accepted connection, then **null** — hide the card.

Empty `announcement.text` means no banner; null `map_image` means no map. Neither is an error.

exec: console.log('quick_start:', qs ? qs.step + ' ' + qs.progress + '/' + qs.target : 'done — card hidden');

item.name: 5. Missions, QR codes & leaderboard
item.description: XP is awarded **server-side only**. Saving a session and accepting a connection award their missions through database triggers; scanning a QR code awards through `POST user/qr/scan`. There is no route that completes a mission on request, and `user_missions` is no longer client-writable (a REST write returns 42501).

request.description:
The catalog plus my progress: `is_completed`, `times_completed` (the "Times Completed" counter), `xp_earned`, `remaining` and a `how_to_earn` hint.

`summary.mission_xp` counts missions only; `summary.total_xp` also counts session check-ins, so the two are not expected to match.

`include_inactive=true` also returns missions with `is_active = false`.

exec: // Repeatable missions are the ones with a counter worth watching.

request.description:
Claim a printed code. `code` is the slug from `https://<app>/q/<code>` — the whole scanned URL is accepted too, and `?code=` works instead of a body.

Mint codes to print with `select * from public.mint_qr_codes('zone', 'Zone', 8, 'explore_zone');` then set the `qr_code` collection variable to one of the returned slugs.

**A repeat scan is a 200, not an error** — `counted: false` with `"You have already scanned this one."`. Branch on `counted`, not the status code. 404 = unknown code, 409 = code switched off.

exec: console.log('Set the qr_code variable to a real slug from mint_qr_codes():', body.message);

request.description:
Rankings by XP — mission XP plus session check-in XP, admins excluded.

`per_page` defaults to **15** (the top-15 board) and pages like every other list. `me` is the caller's own card for the panel underneath, always present even when they are also in `entries` (`is_me` marks that row).

Someone who has earned nothing is **unranked** (`rank: null`, `total_xp: 0`) rather than ranked last. `user_id` is what `GET user/profile/{id}` takes, for tapping a name.
Read-only. `code` is the stable machine name the triggers and QR codes reference — prefer it over the id or the title.

One row per completion that counted, own rows only. `source_key` is the dedup key — `agenda:<uuid>`, `qr:<id>`, `connection:<uuid>`, `derived:all` — which is why re-adding a session never counts twice.

item.name: 6. Agenda
item.description:
Every event carries the caller's own state (`my_status`, `is_saved`, `is_checked_in`) and `is_past`, so a list screen needs one call.

Tags are `public.guilds` rows: at most two per event, one primary. `quest_section` is `main` / `side` / `bonus`.

**`user_agenda` is no longer client-writable** — use `POST user/agenda/schedule`. A direct REST insert or delete returns 42501.

request.description:
Filters, all optional: `day` (a date `YYYY-MM-DD` **or** a configs.id of type `event-day`), `quest` (`main` / `side` / `bonus` / a configs.id), `guild_id` (tag), `user_type` (Builder / Operator / Explorer), `search` (name, speaker, company, location), `saved=true`, `sponsored=true`. `all` means no filter.

Chronological order. Past events are **returned, not hidden** — grey them out using `is_past`.

exec: // Remember one of each kind, so the save / interest requests below have a target.
console.log('No events yet — seed public.agenda first.');

request.description:
The day tabs, with `event_count` / `saved_count` per day.

Open on `current_day`: today if the conference is running, otherwise the next day still to come, otherwise the last one — so the screen is never blank.

**Pass `today` as the client's own local date.** Left out, the server's UTC date decides, and a US conference would flip over mid-afternoon.

Same `events` shape as the list above, so one renderer serves both.

`status`: `scheduled` (default — saved + approved), `saved`, `interested` (waiting on an admin for an invite-only event), `approved`, `rejected`, `all`. Takes every filter the main list takes.

item.name: Add a session to my schedule

request.description:
`action`: `save` | `unsave` | `interest` | `withdraw` (also accepted as `?action=`).

Saving a **Main/Side Quest** earns the "Add a session" mission; saving a **Bonus Quest** (offsite) earns "Book Your First Quest". `missions` in the response is the progress *after* the write, so the counter can move without a second call.

409 on an invite-only event — use `interest`. Repeating an action you have already taken answers 200 with the current state.

item.name: Remove a session (re-adding will NOT count again)

request.description:
`unsave` (or `withdraw` for an interest request) deletes the row.

The mission completion is keyed on the event, so removing does **not** decrement the counter and re-adding does **not** increment it — the FRD's "removing and re-adding the same session will not count". Run this then re-run the save above to see the counter hold steady.

For events with `is_invite_only = true`, where the Agenda screen shows this instead of add-to-schedule. Leaves `my_status: "interested"` until an admin approves.

409 on an open event — use `save`. Approving is admin-side and has no route yet: an admin sets `public.user_agenda.status` to `approved`, which awards the mission XP through the same trigger.
The same object as one element of the list. 404 if the id is unknown, 400 if it is not a UUID (`days` and `schedule` are matched as routes first, so they are never read as ids).

Still readable directly. `agenda` has three separate FKs to `configs`, so an embedded `configs(...)` is ambiguous — name the constraint, as below. Tags come through `agenda_guilds(is_primary, guilds(name))`.

item.name: 7. Chat
item.description:
The four chat endpoints. Run them in order the first time: Create stores `chat_id` for Details and Send.

`other_user_id` comes from **People (directory)** in folder 3.

Membership is checked on every route, so a chat you are not in answers 404. New messages arriving while a screen is open come over realtime on `chat_messages` — these endpoints are for loading and sending.

request.description:
Start a chat with an attendee — this is the "Message" button.

Find-or-create: one direct chat per pair, so tapping twice opens the same conversation (`created` tells you which happened, and the message reads "Chat opened."). No connection request is needed first.

`other_user_id` is set by People (directory) in folder 3.

exec: console.log('Run People (directory) first to set other_user_id:', body.message);

request.description:
Every chat I am in, most recently active first, paged.

Each row carries the other person's card, `last_message` (null for a chat with no messages yet) and `unread_count` — messages from them since I last opened it.

`search` matches the other person by name, nerd number, company or job title.

The chat, the other person, and a page of messages **newest first** — page 1 is what the screen opens on, so reverse the array to render oldest-at-top and fetch page 2 for older history.

Opening a chat marks it read; the `unread_count` in the response is the count from before that, so the badge can be cleared from the same payload.

404 if the chat does not exist or you are not a participant.

Posts a message to a chat I am in and answers with the stored row (`is_mine` is always true here).

Up to 4000 characters; empty is a 400. Sending also marks the chat read for the sender.

item.name: 8. Notifications
item.description:
Rows are written server-side only — the app can list, mark read and delete, never create.

`type` is one of `chat_message`, `mission`, `agenda`, `announcement`; `data` carries the deep-link target, e.g. `{"chat_id": "..."}`.

**`read_at` is the only column the app may write.** Patching title/body/data returns 42501 by design, so send `{ read_at }` alone rather than the whole object.

request.description: Your notifications, newest first (there's an index for exactly this). Stores the first id in `notification_id`.

exec: else console.log('No notifications yet — nothing is inserting them until push delivery is built.');

request.description:
HEAD + `Prefer: count=exact` returns the count in the `Content-Range` header (`0-0/1`) without transferring rows. In supabase-js: `.select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true }).is('read_at', null)`.

Backed by a partial index on unread rows.

Send `read_at` only. Adding `title`, `body` or `data` to this body returns **42501 permission denied for table notifications** — column-level grants stop a user rewriting a notification they were sent.
The `read_at=is.null` filter is the whole mark-all-read operation; RLS keeps it to your own rows. Returns 204.
Returns 204. Deleting a notification that isn't yours silently affects 0 rows.

item.name: 9. Admin routes
item.description:
Admin-only routes on one edge function, routed on the path: GET admin/user/list, POST admin/user/add, DELETE admin/user/remove, GET admin/announcement/get, POST admin/announcement/post.

user/* manages public.email_stack (the invite list registration is gated on); announcement/* edits the banner every signed-in user sees.

**Admin only**: needs the access token of a user whose public.users row has is_admin = true. Run **1. Auth → Login** with an admin account first; these requests inherit that token.

is_admin is writable only by the service role (Studio or SQL), so an admin cannot promote anyone through the API:

```sql
update public.users set is_admin = true where email = 'you@yourdomain.com';
```

Entries are invitations, not accounts: removing one stops future registrations but leaves any account that already registered with it untouched.

request.description:
Paged, searchable view of the invite list.

| Query parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| page | integer | 1 | 1-based |
| per_page | integer | 50 | Capped at 200 |
| search | string | — | Case-insensitive substring of the email. `%` and `_` match literally, not as wildcards |
| limit / offset | integer | — | Accepted as aliases, if you prefer that style |

**200**

```json
{
  "status": "Success",
  "message": "7 emails on the attendee list.",
  "data": {
    "users": [{ "id": "...", "email": "ada@example.com", "first_name": "Ada", "last_name": null }],
    "search": null,
    "pagination": { "total": 7, "page": 1, "per_page": 3, "total_pages": 3, "has_next": true, "has_prev": false }
  }
}
```

`pagination.total` counts what the filter matched, so it drives the pager even with a `search` active. A page past the end is not an error — it returns an empty `users` array with the real totals.

exec: console.log('admin route:', pm.response.code, body.message, '- log in as a user with is_admin = true to run this.');

request.description:
| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| email | string | one of the two | A single address |
| emails | array | one of the two | Up to 200. Items may be strings or `{ email, first_name?, last_name? }` |
| first_name | string | no | Only with the single-`email` form |
| last_name | string | no | Only with the single-`email` form |

Addresses are trimmed and lower-cased; matching ignores case, so `NINA@Example.com` and `nina@example.com` are the same entry.

- **200** `data: { requested, added_count, added[], already_on_list[] }`
- **400** one invalid address rejects the whole request and nothing is written
- **401** no bearer token, or the anon key was sent instead of a user's
- **403** signed in but `is_admin` is false
- **404** unknown route — the message lists the valid ones
- **405** wrong method for the route

request.description:
Saves the announcement banner and/or the Home floor plan.

- `text` — up to 2000 characters. **May be empty**: an empty string (or `null`, or whitespace only) clears the banner, which is how an admin turns it off.
- `map_image` — public `http(s)` URL of the floor plan shown on Home. `null` or `""` removes the map. Upload the image to a storage bucket first; this stores the URL, not the bytes.

Both are optional so they can be edited independently, but sending **neither** is a 400 — a client bug cannot blank the banner by accident, while clearing it stays an explicit action.

Users read both fields from `GET user/home`, or over REST from `announcements`.

item.name: 10. Announcement
item.description:
The event-wide banner, as users read it: a single row in public.announcements, readable by any signed-in user. Admins edit it through **9. Admin routes**.

Empty `text` means there is no announcement — hide the banner rather than rendering an empty bar.

request.description:
Returns an array with the single announcement row:

```json
[{ "text": "Keynote moved to 10am.", "updated_at": "2026-08-19T11:00:29.927669+00:00" }]
```

In supabase-js, `.select('text, updated_at').single()` gives you the object directly.

Needs a session — the select policy is `to authenticated`, so without one this is a 401. Writes are rejected on this path for everyone, admins included.

item.name: Z. Not used by the app (direct REST)
item.description:
Kept for debugging and for anyone poking at the tables directly. The app should call the edge functions instead:

- guilds / configs → **2. Config** (`GET config`)
- chat create / participants / messages → **7. Chat** (`chat/create`, `chat/list`, `chat/details/{id}`, `chat/send/{id}`)

These still work — the RLS policies allow them — but the function routes do the multi-step writes in one transaction and return the shapes the screens need. See postman/API.md §8.6.
